{"section_id":"MA-S4","heading_text":"","section_markdown":"## Training objective: InfoNCE loss with fixed query anchor.

The training objective of the dedicated attention model is the InfoNCE contrastive loss computed with a fixed query anchor. In this formulation, the query-side representation is held constant across the positive and negative similarity evaluations, while the document-side representations are varied to form the contrastive set. The model's forward pass produces per-sample loss values that are aggregated into a scalar training signal, and the objective is structured so that the anchor query serves as the reference point against which both positive and negative document similarities are measured.

When the positional-encoding configuration flag is enabled, the passage representation is computed by combining the document-level embedding with the passage-level embedding, yielding a unified passage tensor that carries both granularities of identity. The positive and negative similarity vectors are then concatenated into a single similarity tensor of length equal to the sum of the positive and negative counts, forming the contrastive set over which the InfoNCE denominator is evaluated. A guard branch inspects whether the per-sample loss tensor has zero entries; in that case the routine emits diagnostic output listing the positive mask, negative mask, similarity values, labels, and the concatenated similarity vector for the affected sample. Under normal operation the aggregated loss is returned as the scalar output of the forward pass.

The fixed query anchor is realized by reusing a single query-side representation across all contrastive evaluations within a training step. Rather than re-encoding the query for each candidate document, the model computes the query embedding once and pairs it against the set of positive and negative document embeddings to form the similarity matrix. This design choice keeps the computational cost of the query side constant with respect to the number of negatives, and it ensures that the contrastive signal isolates the document-side discriminative capacity.

The positive and negative similarity values are assembled into a unified tensor before the InfoNCE log-partition is computed. The positive similarities correspond to document passages whose identifiers match the query's associated chunk, while the negative similarities are drawn from passages that do not satisfy this identifier-matching condition. The concatenated similarity vector thus spans the full contrastive set, and the InfoNCE loss is the negative log-likelihood of the positive entries under the softmax over the entire vector.

The loss is computed per sample and then reduced to a scalar by averaging across the batch dimension. Each sample contributes one positive and a configurable number of negatives, so the per-sample InfoNCE value reflects the local contrastive difficulty for that query. The batch-level scalar is the arithmetic mean of these per-sample values, which serves as the gradient signal for the optimizer. The diagnostic branch that fires when a sample yields no positive passages indicates a data-integrity condition in which the identifier-matching criterion was not satisfied for any candidate document.

The returned scalar loss is the direct input to the training optimizer. Because the query anchor is fixed within a step, the gradient flows only through the document-side embedding parameters and the attention weights that modulate their interaction with the query. This asymmetry means that the query representation is learned in a separate or preceding training phase, and the contrastive objective here refines the document-side geometry to align with the already-learned query space.
